title: Conquering Agent Chaos — Rick Blalock, Agentuity
talk_summary: This is largely a product demo of Agentuity's agent-native deployment platform (CLI, YAML config, containerized runtimes, built-in AI gateway, per-agent cost/session tracing, decoupled input channels like email/SMS/cron). The only transferable ideas are architectural: treat agents as first-class deployable units with long-running/pausable execution, and surface per-agent/per-run cost and session traces.

takeaways.technique: Agents as first-class infra citizens with long-running, pausable execution
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent is deployed as its own containerized unit with routing handled by the platform, explicitly designed to run as long as needed and pause/resume rather than fit serverless timeouts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they need to run as long as they need to run. Um and they need to be able to pause and stop and resume
takeaways.numbers: internal agent runs 40 minutes a day

takeaways.technique: Per-agent/per-run cost and session tracing surfaced in one place
takeaways.what_they_do: Platform records every model call with prompt, response, and cost, aggregated by project, agent, and run, and mirrors the same view in dev and prod.

takeaways.technique: Ephemeral scoped tokens for agent-to-agent calls
takeaways.what_they_do: When one agent calls another, the platform issues an ephemeral token valid only for the duration of that run, rather than sharing long-lived keys.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We'll get an ephemeral token so it's allowed to talk to it for as long as it runs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents accept multiple input types (webhook, email, SMS, cron, JSON/PDF) routed onto a single request handler, so the same agent is triggered by many sources.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can decouple inputs and outputs from your agent ... I can say, 'Hey, I want to give my agent an email.'
